turns:
Create a new Python CLI tool called `todo.py` in this directory. Standard library only.

Spec — the quoted user-facing messages are exact literals; reproduce them character-for-character:
- `python3 todo.py add "<text>"` → append to todos.json, print "added: #<id> <text>"
- `python3 todo.py list` → print pending items as `#<id> [ ] <text>` and completed items as `#<id> [x] <text>`, ordered by id
- `python3 todo.py done <id>` → mark complete, print "done: #<id>". For a nonexistent id, print "error: no such id" and exit with code 1
- `python3 todo.py rm <id>` → delete, print "removed: #<id>". For a nonexistent id, same error handling as above
- ids are integers starting from 1 and are never reused, even after deletion
- If todos.json doesn't exist, create it automatically; if it contains broken JSON, print "error: corrupt save file" and exit with code 2

Acceptance tests live in `tests/test_cli.py`. The goal is to pass `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

rubric.name: Spec compliance
rubric.desc: All commands, output formats, and exit codes exact

rubric.name: Code quality
rubric.desc: Clean CLI structure and error handling

turns:
`data/sales_raw.csv` contains messy sales data. Write a cleaning script `clean.py`
and run it to produce `data/sales_clean.csv`.

Cleaning rules:
- Columns: date,product,qty,unit_price (keep the header)
- date comes in mixed formats (2026-07-01, 2026/07/01, 01-07-2026, etc.) → normalize all of them to YYYY-MM-DD. Drop rows that can't be parsed
- Drop rows where qty is empty, non-numeric, or 0 or less
- Strip commas and the ₩ currency symbol from unit_price and convert to an integer (e.g. "₩12,000" → 12000). Drop rows that can't be parsed
- Trim leading/trailing whitespace from product; keep only one copy of exact duplicate rows (all 4 fields identical)
- After cleaning, sort by date, then product

When you're done, tell me how many rows remain.

rubric.desc: Accuracy of the result report, e.g. remaining row count
